Swamp Talker is the murloc Bengor names as having seized the Warchief’s Orders during an ambush on the way to the Blasted Lands. Bengor places Swamp Talker in a cave to the east.
Grimnal is a mail and plate merchant in the Swamp of Sorrows who sells goods and repairs equipment.
Hartash is a weapon merchant in the Swamp of Sorrows who sells goods and repairs equipment.
Thultash is a food and drink vendor in the Swamp of Sorrows.
Thultazor is an alchemy supplies and reagent merchant. His local role is to sell goods to visitors browsing his stock.
Thralosh sells cloth and leather armor and also offers repairs. Those services make him a practical stop for travelers seeking equipment or its upkeep.

Malosh trains warriors. His opening remarks can be brusque: he asks whether a visitor wants training or is wasting a warrior’s time, and another conditional response rejects a character of the visitor’s kind. The exchange depends on context, so it does not establish a universal refusal.

Haromm trains shamans and greets visitors by saying the spirits guided them to him. He also directs a shaman to Bath’rah the Windwatcher with a request to bring samples of the four elements, framing the journey as a summons for someone of the visitor’s wisdom.

Ogromm trains hunters. His brief conditional replies—“What?” and “Don’t waste my time.”—give his exchanges a curt edge, while the available options also cover retraining and dual talent specialization.

Kartosh trains warlocks and speaks with contempt about a woman he says believes herself the new mistress of Stonard, sarcastically suggesting her succubi could help clean up her messes. He also sends a warlock to Impsy in Felwood at the imp’s request; his account asks for felcloth as a sign of good faith. The evidence does not identify the woman in his remark.
Banalash is a Trade Supplies merchant who offers goods to browse.
Mire Lord is a powerful creature whose combat behavior includes casting a spell when injured.
Sawtooth Snapper is a crocolisk wildlife creature. Its combat behavior includes a spell cast when injured.
A monstrous crawler found in the wetlands of Dustwallow Marsh. Its combat script casts a spell while fighting.
A Lost One cook encountered in Dustwallow Marsh. The records identify the creature as an elite, but give no further detail about its cooking or personal history.

Rogvar is Stonard’s alchemy trainer, sent there at Thrall’s request. He values the herbs growing in the marsh but misses the quiet before the elves arrived. Irritated by nearby commotion, he grumbles about earplugs and calls a woman’s methods cowardly, comparing them to those of Forsaken apothecaries.

Helgrum the Swift is a Stonard scout who relies on communication with Kargath’s head scout, Neeka Bloodscar. He sends an outrunner to collect her report on the Badlands outpost and uses it to judge the Alliance’s difficulties and the possibility of shared enemies.

Fel'zerul is a Horde investigator in Stonard, studying the strange events at the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar and the magic behind them. He regards Jammal'an's belief in Hakkar's return as dangerous folly, and fears the enchanted fetishes may enable the Atal'ai summoning ritual. He studies recovered artifacts, then destroys the fetishes as instruments of evil.
Zun'dartha, a humanoid in the Swamp of Sorrows.

Magtoor helps lead the Draenei at the Harborage, where stolen sacred draenethyst crystals matter to the community's ability to endure after its journey to Azeroth. The Harborage is vulnerable: Magtoor says they fear being crushed by nearby Stonard and lack the strength to confront the Lost Ones, who threaten them and took the crystals.
Grokor is a pet trainer who helps hunters train their pets. He says he only helps hunters and their pets.
Moccasin is a critter found across several areas.

An elven ally of Ysera's Dragonflight, Itharius is committed to redeeming Eranikus. The oathstone he offers sets out a serious charge: aid the dragonflight and relinquish the gem holding what remains of Eranikus's free will. To reach Eranikus through the tainted gem, Itharius sends the mortal to seek Umbranse, a human medium in Winterspring. He believes choices matter, while leaving the decision to the mortal he addresses.

Galen Goodward begs for help escaping creatures he fears will eat him. He offers treasure from his camp north of Stonard in return, keeping the strongbox's opening trick secret until he is helped to safety. He expresses lasting gratitude to his rescuer.

Infiltrator Marksen pleads for mercy, claiming to know political treachery that crosses alliance boundaries despite having no sympathy for the Horde. Marksen believes the Forsaken are misleading the Horde's allies and is willing to share that suspicion. An eagerly accepted drink contains Faustin's serum mixed into ale; Marksen's account gives way to dizziness and pain.

Watcher Biggs is the sole survivor of a caravan attacked by Lost Ones, sworn to protect its remaining supplies. Biggs seeks stolen reagents for Nethergarde's wizards and dry wood to repair the wagon. Though the wizards' work is linked to the Dark Portal and Alliance security, Biggs does not know its details and depends on help to continue the journey.
Noboru the Cudgel is accused of persecuting the draenei of the Harborage for months. His cudgel is described as a symbol of the brutality they have suffered at the hands of the Lost Ones.
Zuul serves as a grunt.
Tharlak serves as a grunt.

Dar is an orc who supplies meat to customers and arranges food shipments for Tok'Kar's coastal outpost. He asks for crawler legs to send back to his customers and has not had time to arrange another shipment of sawtooth meat for the outpost.

Tok'Kar helps run the coastal camp that guards against murlocs and warns Stonard when threats are too large to face. He cooks for his soldiers, seeks supplies to make camp life easier, and crafts weapons from sawtooth snapper claws for the fight. He directs visitors to Katar for beach patrols and appreciates help that lifts Katar's spirits.

Katar despises the sea and its murlocs, taking pleasure in their deaths and encouraging others to share that hatred. Katar vows to keep them beyond the borders, rewards continued attacks against them, and directs successful fighters to Tok'Kar for weapons. This hostility goes beyond a practical defense: Katar wishes for an army to eradicate the fish men everywhere.
Ongeku is identified as a Lost One in the Swamp of Sorrows who holds a shard of draenethyst sought by Uthek the Wise to strengthen Uthek's magic.
Breyk is a wind rider master who handles flight route requests. If attacked, he calls for guards and summons an enraged wyvern.
Karakul is an innkeeper who sees the inn as a place for weary fighters to rest and share battle stories. He also offers lodging and goods.

Once a Horde commander, the Fallen Hero carries the guilt of a disastrous decision that cost his regiment many soldiers. Captured and tortured after returning to the Blasted Lands, he now seeks to rescue his men's tormented souls and restore his honor. He calls adventurers to free them and oppose the Shadowsworn and Razelikh's forces. Though he remembers the Horde and its losses, he is willing to unite with the Alliance against their common enemy.

Dispatch Commander Ruag is a Horde commander in Stonard who handles the regiment's missing orders. He says he relayed them, but the soldiers carrying them were ambushed by murlocs; only one survived, gravely disabled. The regiment's destruction still weighs on him, and he remembers its soldiers as some of the Horde's best. When questioned, he warns visitors to mind their business, suggesting he is guarded about the affair.

Bengor is the battered survivor of an ambush on the way to Blasted Lands. He recalls murlocs taking the orders he carried, including one called the Swamp Talker; his account trails off as he passes out.
Corporal Thund Splithoof honors heroes of old. He recognizes a visitor's nobility and heroism as honoring others too, then gives thanks on behalf of those honored.
Gharash supplies blacksmithing goods and repairs equipment in the Swamp of Sorrows.
Rartar sells alchemy supplies in the Swamp of Sorrows.
Jarquia is a combatant whose battle behavior includes becoming enraged when badly hurt.
Hekkru is a stable master whose role includes pet stabling and help recovering lost companions.
A humanoid known as the Broken Exile in Swamp of Sorrows.
Masat T'andr is a superior leatherworker who offers goods for sale.
Greshka voices a pointed remark about an unnamed woman.
Somnus is an ancient green dragon of the Green Flight, described as its drake champion. Accounts place him at the Pool of Tears with his dragonkin.
Sawfin Frenzy is a beast.
Lord Captain Wyrmak is a named dragon boss. His title identifies him as a captain.
Fingat is a humanoid found in the Blasted Lands and Swamp of Sorrows.
Gilmorian is a humanoid.
Molt Thorn is an elemental.

Cersei Dusksinger is an ambitious warlock and experimenter at Stonard, where she plots against the draenei and resents the orcs for leaving nearby power untapped. She experiments on the Lost Ones and plans to curse their captured livestock with fel-tainted food, hoping to strike at Anchorite Avuun and the draenei. Her words show open contempt for Avuun and confidence that her scheme will go undiscovered; she treats the work as entertainment as well as revenge.
A jaguar held captive by the Lost Ones, one of the animals Cersei Dusksinger targets in her fel-tainted food experiment.
A tarantula held captive by the Lost Ones, one of the animals Cersei Dusksinger targets in her fel-tainted food experiment.

A crocolisk held as livestock by the Lost Ones at Fallow Sanctuary. Cersei Dusksinger intends to curse the Lost Ones by feeding their captured animals fel-tainted morsels; this crocolisk is among the animals targeted in her scheme.

One of the Lost Ones further corrupted by fel energies, according to Anchorite Avuun. Avuun believes these cursed creatures should be spared further suffering, though he sees no remedy for those already so corrupted. Cursed Lost Ones are found near Fallow Sanctuary.

Anchorite Avuun is a draenei scholar staying with Magtoor while studying the Lost Ones of Fallow Sanctuary. He hopes to cure their fel corruption and believes the same knowledge could help the Broken. Compassionate toward the Lost Ones, he considers mercy appropriate when corruption leaves no hope of recovery, and he regards dealings with the Horde with contempt.
A draenei protector.

Holaaru is one of the Broken, explaining that fel energies transformed the original draenei form less severely than happened to the Lost Ones. At the Harborage, Holaaru eagerly studies Azeroth's past and seeks Atal'ai artifacts from the Pool of Tears to understand that civilization. Learning the world's history is, for Holaaru, a way for Broken and draenei to fit in.

The Swamp of Sorrows Flame Keeper welcomes visitors to honor the local festival flame and the fires of other Horde settlements. The keeper dismisses Alliance fires as unworthy and urges their desecration.

Lorrin Foxfire trains mages in portal travel at Stonard. Initially resentful of the posting and disdainful of the Horde’s ways, Lorrin came to appreciate the local culture, humidity and even the smell of orc sweat and rot. Lorrin praises immersion in another culture and the benefits of mud and moisture for the complexion, while pondering whether the assignment reflected special aptitude or a rumor of talking too much.

place_records.text: You are in the Swamp of Sorrows, a Horde-held swamp in the Eastern Kingdoms. The Horde holds it in places, with Stonard its only settlement, and no Alliance settlement stands here. Deathstrike tarantulas, swamp jaguars and tangled horrors roam the swamp, and the Lost Ones catch or kill those who wander near Fallow Sanctuary. Murlocs strike the coast, and Atal'ai trolls haunt the sunken temple by the Pool of Tears.

You are in Pool of Tears, a sunken-temple area of the Swamp of Sorrows. The Atal'ai temple sank here, and Atal'ai trolls, mummified and enthralled, still prowl its shores with sawfin frenzies in the water. A Horde explorer from Stonard is found here too.

You are in Stonard, the Horde's settlement in the Swamp of Sorrows. Haromm trains shamans and Kartosh trains warlocks here. Cersei Dusksinger, an ambitious warlock, experiments on the Lost Ones, while Dispatch Commander Ruag still grieves a regiment ruined when murlocs took its orders. Its inn serves travellers.

You are in Fallow Sanctuary, where the Lost Ones keep captured animals as livestock. Their hunters, muckdwellers and a chieftain roam here and catch or kill those who wander near. Cersei Dusksinger plans to curse the captured crocolisk and other animals with fel-tainted food.
You are in Misty Valley, part of the Swamp of Sorrows. Swampwalkers, tangled horrors, a swampwalker elder and a mire lord roam here.

You are in Misty Reed Strand, a beach on the Swamp of Sorrows coast. Marsh murlocs, inkspewers and oracles come ashore here. Katar, a Horde figure who despises the sea, rewards those who kill its murlocs and sends fighters to Tok'Kar for weapons.

You are in The Harborage, a draenei community in the Swamp of Sorrows. Magtoor leads it, and its people fear being crushed by nearby Stonard while the Lost Ones of Fallow Sanctuary hold their stolen draenethyst crystals. Anchorite Avuun, a draenei scholar, studies those Lost Ones in hope of curing them.

You are in Itharius's Cave, where Itharius, an elven ally of Ysera's Dragonflight, works to redeem Eranikus, the dragon held within a gem. Adolescent whelps, dreaming whelps and swamp jaguars haunt the cave.

You are in Sorrowmurk, where a spirit healer offers a return to life for a price, though it may not yet be the traveller's time. Lord Captain Wyrmak, elder dragonkin, Scalebane captains and mummified Atal'ai roam nearby.
You are in Splinterspear Junction, a crossroads in the Swamp of Sorrows. A spirit healer and a Horde scout from Stonard are here, and sorrow spinners roam the area.
You are in Stagalbog, where an Alliance Nethergarde miner works. Deathstrike tarantulas, marsh inkspewers, marsh flesheaters, marsh oracles and a fingat roam the area.
You are in The Shifting Mire, part of the Swamp of Sorrows. Swamp jaguars, molt thorns, sorrow spinners and Lost Ones roam here, and a Horde explorer from Stonard is found here too.

You are in Misty Reed Post, the Horde's coastal camp in the Swamp of Sorrows that guards against murlocs and warns Stonard of threats too large to face. Tok'Kar, who helps run the camp, crafts weapons from sawtooth snapper claws. A Stonard hunter and shaman are here too.
You are in The Forbidding Sea, the open water of the Swamp of Sorrows. Sawtooth snappers, coral sharks and marsh inkspewers hunt its waters, and marsh flesheaters prowl here too.
You are in Stagalbog Cave, a cave in the Swamp of Sorrows. Marsh flesheaters, marsh oracles and marsh inkspewers haunt it, and Fingat roams here too.
